query: Single-phase fcc FeCoNi has high saturation magnetization but a low coercive field, and reported single-phase fcc high-entropy alloys derived from it have coercive fields no greater than 100 Oe in the reported magnetic measurements. What single intervention could overcome this coercivity limitation? Formulate one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its mechanism, the predicted change relative to single-phase fcc FeCoNi or a matched derivative, the relevant compositional, structural, and measurement boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled experiment with an explicit falsification criterion.

generation.hypothesis: Adding a small amount of Sn to single‐phase fcc FeCoNi will trigger the formation of nanoscale secondary (BCC) precipitates within the fcc matrix that act as domain wall pinning sites, increasing the coercivity beyond 100 Oe relative to the pure fcc alloy.
generation.material_initial_state: Single-phase fcc FeCoNi (or a closely related derivative) with high saturation magnetization and coercivity below 100 Oe.
generation.intervention: Incorporate a minor Sn addition (on the order of a few atomic percent, up to ~10 at.%) during alloy synthesis.
generation.conditions: Arc-melted alloy followed by controlled cooling to achieve a mixed-phase microstructure; magnetic measurements performed near room temperature.
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of nanoscale BCC precipitates dispersed in the fcc matrix.
generation.mechanism: The Sn addition destabilizes the single-phase fcc structure slightly, promoting a limited BCC-phase precipitation. The nanoscale BCC precipitates serve as effective pinning centers for magnetic domain walls, which impedes domain wall motion and thereby raises the coercive field.
generation.predicted_outcome: An increase in coercivity to values significantly above 100 Oe compared to the baseline single-phase fcc FeCoNi, with saturation magnetization remaining relatively high.
generation.baseline: The magnetic properties (coercivity < 100 Oe and high saturation magnetization) of a single-phase fcc FeCoNi or matched derivative.
generation.boundary: The study is limited to near-equiatomic FeCoNi compositions with minor Sn additions (e.g., up to ~10 at.%), synthesized via arc-melting with controlled cooling, and magnetic properties measured at ambient temperature.
generation.uncertainty: The precise Sn concentration needed for optimal coercivity increase and the potential trade-offs with other magnetic properties (e.g., saturation magnetization, remanence) are not yet well defined.

falsification_experiment.design: Synthesize a series of FeCoNi alloys with systematically varied Sn content (e.g., 0, 2, 5, and 10 at.%) by arc-melting and controlled cooling. Use X-ray diffraction and transmission electron microscopy to confirm the formation of a dual-phase (fcc + BCC) microstructure. Measure room temperature magnetic hysteresis loops to obtain coercive field values.
measurements: Coercive field (Oe) from hysteresis loop measurements
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the Sn-doped alloys do not show formation of nanoscale BCC precipitates or if the coercivity does not increase significantly compared to the single-phase fcc baseline (i.e., remains below or near 100 Oe), then the hypothesis is falsified.

cited_evidence.text: The present work exhibits the effects of Sn addition on the magnetic properties and microstructure of FeCoNi(CuAl)0.8Snx (0 ≤ x ≤ 0.10) high-entropy alloys (HEAs). The results show all the samples consist of a mixed structure of face-centered-cubic (FCC) phase and body-centered-cubic (BCC) phase. The addition of Sn promotes the formation of BCC phase, and it also affects the shape of Cu-rich nano-precipitates in BCC matrix. It also shows that the Curie temperatures (Tc) of the FCC phase and the saturation magnetization (Ms) of the FeCoNi(CuAl)0.8Snx (0 ≤ x ≤ 0.10) HEAs increase greatly while the remanence (Br) decreases after the addition of Sn into FeCoNi(CuAl)0.8 HEA. The thermomagnetic curves indicate that the phases of the FeCoNi(CuAl)0.8Snx (0 ≤ x ≤ 0.10) HEAs will transform from FCC with low Tc to BCC phase with high Tc at temperature of 600–700 K. This work provides a new idea for FeCoNi(CuAl)0.8Snx (0 ≤ x ≤ 0.10) HEAs for their potential application as soft magnets to be used at high temperatures.

Recently, the magnetic properties of HEAs with varying composition have been extensively investigated. The CuAl contents had obvious influence on the microstructure and saturation magnetization of FeCoNi(CuAl)x alloy, and the Ms of FeCoNi(CuAl)0.8 alloy increased from 78.9 Am2 kg−1 to 93.1 Am2 kg−1 by annealing at 673 K. Annealing can effectively improve the saturation magnetization of a certain constituent. Zhang et al. have prepared the FeCoNi(SiAl)x HEAs by arc-melting method and found that the electrical resistivity increased and sacrificed the magnetization with adding SiAl content, and the coercivity with a single-phase structure (BCC or FCC) was smaller than that of the two-phase structure (BCC and FCC). Therefore, the alloy components and annealing process have great influence on the magnetic properties of alloys. In addition, Chen et al. found that the electrical conductivity of FeCoNiCrAlx alloys decreased as x increasing in single-phase (FCC or BCC) regions and the electrical conductivity in duplex phase region possessed smaller value than that in single region.
